news.lede: Jamie Carragher talked about being approached by the legendary Arsenal manager, who has since joined FIFA, to endorse a proposal many fans were against. FIFA as an organisation have come under fire over the last few months, despite the enormous success of the FIFA World Cup this summer. Gianni Infantino’s attempt to privatise the FIFA World Cup through a subsidiary was instantly rejected. But years ago, FIFA tried floating a far more controversial idea, one helmed by one of football’s great managers.

news.title: Billionaire Patrice Motsepe and CAF executives backs Infantino after FIFA drops plan to "sell the World Cup" for $4.2 billion
news.lede: Patrice Motsepe, the billionaire president of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), has spearheaded a wave of support for FIFA President Gianni Infantino despite a growing rift in global football governance. This surge of loyalty from the continent follows Infantino’s decision to abandon a controversial proposal to raise $4.2 billion by selling minority stakes in a new commercial rights body. While regional bodies in Europe, Asia, and North America have recently declared a loss of confidence in Infantino’s leadership, the 54-member African bloc remains his most vital base of political power heading into the next FIFA presidential election. The controversy centered on a project known as the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a proposed $20 billion subsidiary designed to manage the World Cup and other major events.

news.title: The Club World Cup deals the knockout blow to Infantino
news.lede: Aleksander Ceferin, president of European football's governing body (UEFA), and Nasser Al-Khelaifi, chairman of the European Club Association, are holding an anticipated meeting in the city of Salzburg. Tension is rising between their organisations and world football's governing body (FIFA), specifically against its president Gianni Infantino. According to the "talkSPORT" network, the root of that tension lies in the possibility of the European clubs withdrawing from the 2029 Club World Cup, following UEFA's decision regarding the national teams in relation to the World Cup. Spanish newspaper "AS" reported that there is as yet no agreement between the European Club Association and FIFA to stage the 2029 Club World Cup, which makes talk of boycotting the tournament inaccurate for now.

news.title: Oliver Baumann says Julian Nagelsmann apologized after World Cup benching
news.lede: Germany goalkeeper Oliver Baumann has opened up about one of the toughest moments of his career after Julian Nagelsmann opted to restore Manuel Neuer as the starting goalkeeper for the World Cup. Baumann had established himself as Germany’s No. 1 leading up to the tournament, but Nagelsmann, leaning on input from some key players, ultimately turned back to Neuer for football’s biggest stage. While the decision was undoubtedly disappointing for Baumann, the goalkeeper sayid that the ex-Germany coach, who was recently replaced by Jürgen Klopp, reached out afterward to discuss everything openly. “He [Nagelsmann] was sorry about how everything turned out in the end.

FIFA’s chief of global football development Arsene Wenger says Gianni Infantino’s decision to withdraw from a plan to sell stakes in a World Cup company to private investors was “absolutely necessary and beyond question”. Former Arsenal manager Wenger issued a statement on Tuesday morning a week on from the first reports emerging about Infantino’s plan to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) and sell a 20 per cent stake in it to private equity.
